skill.name: Draft a Commit
skill.description: Draft clear commit messages from staged Git changes with configurable tone and format.
skill.summary: Generate reviewable commit message drafts from staged changes.
skill.author: AbeJitsu

content.value_statement: Staged changes can be hard to summarize clearly. This skill reviews the staged diff and drafts a readable commit message.
actual_capabilities: Reviews staged changes using git diff --cached.
Infers work type such as feature, fix, docs, test, or refactor.
Drafts descriptive or conventional commit messages.
Supports concise or detailed message styles through configuration.
Can include explanatory context and file count summaries.
limitations: The skill does not stage files, create commits, or modify repositories.
Ambiguous diffs may require user clarification.
Configuration changes require editing the project config file.

use_cases.title: Summarize Feature Work
use_cases.description: Draft a clear message for a new feature with tests and documentation.

use_cases.title: Prepare Review Commits
use_cases.description: Create focused commit messages before sharing changes with a team.

use_cases.title: Standardize Release History
use_cases.description: Use conventional commit format for cleaner changelogs and release notes.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: You have staged a focused change and need a simple message.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a commit message for my staged changes.

prompt_templates.title: Concise Message
prompt_templates.scenario: You want a short message with only essential context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes and draft a concise commit message with one short context sentence.

prompt_templates.title: Conventional Commit
prompt_templates.scenario: Your project follows conventional commit prefixes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my staged changes and draft a conventional commit message with the best type and scope.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Drafts
prompt_templates.scenario: You want options before choosing the final message.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the staged diff, explain the inferred work type, and provide three commit message options with different detail levels.

output_examples.input: Staged changes add authentication tests and update the login error message.
output_examples.output: Add login authentication coverage. Expands tests around failed login states and clarifies the user-facing error message.

output_examples.input: Staged changes refactor settings storage and update related documentation.
output_examples.output: refactor: simplify settings storage. Centralizes settings persistence and updates documentation for the new flow.

output_examples.input: Staged changes fix an API response bug and add one regression test.
output_examples.output: Fix malformed API error responses. Ensures errors serialize correctly and adds regression coverage for the response middleware.

best_practices: Stage one logical change before requesting a draft.
Review the proposed message before committing it.
Use the conventional format when your project automates changelogs.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a commit message before staging the intended files.
Do not commit the draft without checking the staged diff yourself.
Do not mix unrelated changes into one generated message.

faq.question: Does this skill create the commit?
faq.answer: No. It drafts a message for review, and you create the commit yourself.

faq.question: What changes does it analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes staged changes through git diff --cached.

faq.question: Can it write conventional commits?
faq.answer: Yes. Configure the skill for conventional format or ask for that format in your prompt.

faq.question: Can I change the tone?
faq.answer: Yes. The configuration supports supportive and concise styles.

faq.question: What happens if no files are staged?
faq.answer: The skill should tell you that no staged changes were found and suggest staging files first.

faq.question: Does it modify my repository?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow only reads staged diffs and returns a message draft.
